title: Kitchener Utilities clean energy transition update
subtitle: Council discussed gas utility business options, gas bill surcharges, hydrogen and renewable natural gas, and partnerships before an in-camera session.
overview: At a special meeting, Council held a strategic discussion on Phase 2 of the Kitchener Utilities Clean Energy Transition Strategy. No decision was required on this item. Staff reported that ideas gathered from workshops and earlier engagement were consolidated into four themes and 11 types of business activity. Staff are now forming teams to investigate each one.

Councillors gave feedback on which options to prioritize. Staff said they are not currently exploring a gas bill surcharge. They will keep looking at ways to offer customers more incentives to move away from natural gas, including how any transition work would be funded. The outcome shapes how the city-owned gas utility plans for a lower-carbon future and what it may mean for customers' costs and options.

Council also approved moving into a closed session after the open meeting. It was to consider security of city property with monetary value and a land acquisition matter. The minutes report no other decisions. The meeting adjourned at 3:39 p.m.

decisions.detail: Council agreed to hold a closed session after the meeting on a security of property matter and a land acquisition matter {{vote:m1}}.

debate: One councillor asked why the city was not taking stronger steps, given the Ontario Energy Board's December 2023 statement calling for an end to subsidies for fossil fuel infrastructure in new developments, and noted other cities had backed it. Staff replied that the city's situation differs from Enbridge's. They said its business activities list, including neighbourhood utilities and future gas rates, already reflects these issues.

On a possible gas bill surcharge to fund the transition, staff said they are not exploring one now. They said extra funds could boost incentives under the energy efficiency program. They added that the gas rates theme will look at how transition work is funded and at fixed versus variable charges.

One councillor urged staff to assess early whether hydrogen and renewable natural gas are viable. The councillor said renewable natural gas only reduces carbon and hydrogen may be impractical, and expected the future to be electric. The same councillor suggested working with Kingston, the only other municipality with a gas utility, and with the local electric utility.

Councillors asked what ideas stood out. Staff said many clustered around district energy and thermal energy projects already under way locally. They also described how a neighbourhood utility could move heat between buildings, such as a hospital and a data centre.

A councillor encouraged using the three local post-secondary institutions and their researchers. Staff said these partnerships are already happening, including a hydrogen research group, and that outside consulting support will likely also be needed.
